title: Appliance Repair Leads: How to Get More Calls (2026)
summary: Learn how appliance repair shops get leads: what long-running ads say, which channels bring calls, and how to work out cost per booked job.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Appliance repair leads are mostly phone calls from people with a broken machine who want it fixed today. The shop that answers first and says when a tech can arrive usually gets the job.
- The ads that keep running on[the appliance repair ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/appliance-repair-ads) lean on years in business, a named service area, a starting price and a Call now button. They do not list every machine.
- Best channels: Google Search, Local Services Ads where available, a complete Google Business Profile, then Meta for local awareness and reminders.
- Measure cost per booked job, not clicks or form fills.


## What an appliance repair lead actually is


An appliance repair lead is a person with a dead refrigerator, a washer full of water or an oven that will not heat. They are not browsing. They have food spoiling or laundry piling up, and they want a person on the phone who can say a day and a time.


That changes how appliance repair marketing works. A dental office can run a slow campaign about checkups. A repair shop is paid for speed and trust in the same moment. Most leads arrive as calls, a smaller share as text messages or web forms, and many of them call two or three shops in a row. The first one to pick up and give a clear window tends to win.


Three things decide whether a lead becomes a job.


- **Speed of answer.** A missed call is often a lost job, because the caller dials the next listing.
- **Clarity on price.** People want to know the service call fee and whether it applies to the repair.
- **Proof you are real and local.** Years in business, a town name and reviews settle the doubt about letting a stranger into the house.


## What long-running appliance repair ads have in common


The[appliance repair ad wall](https://www.sprites.ai/appliance-repair-ads) shows 40 live Meta ads from 12 advertisers. The typical ad has been running for a median of 596 days, which is well over a year and a half. Ads rarely run that long unless they keep producing calls, so the long runners are a useful guide to what works for a shop like yours.


About one in five of the ads is video. The rest are images and text. The top button is Call now, on roughly four in ten ads. That fits the trade: the goal is a phone ringing, not a click to a page.


The longest-running ads share a few traits.


What the ads show Why it works for repair


Years in business up front Age signals that the shop will still be there if a repair fails.


Named towns and counties The caller sees that you serve their area, not a national dispatcher.


A starting price It answers the first question before the call and filters out price shoppers early.


Technician already on the way Urgency is the product. The message says help is close, not that you have a nice website.


A call button as the single action One step from the ad to a live person.


Occasional goodwill offers, such as a waived bill for veterans A concrete offer gives people a reason to remember you and share you.


Short lists of symptoms, not long lists of brands The caller recognizes their problem, such as a fridge that is not keeping food fresh.


Two opening lines from the longest-running ads show the pattern. One reads, "Appliance repair experts in the Contra Costa County since 1946." Another reads, "30 years of appliance repair focused on efficient and quality work. Starting at 75.00." The first leads with age and place. The second leads with experience and a price. Neither opens with a discount banner or a list of twenty brands.


## Where appliance repair leads come from


Demand for repair already exists, so the best channels are the ones that catch people at the moment of breakdown. Meta is useful, but it supports search rather than replacing it.


Channel What it does Best use


Google Search ads Shows your shop when someone types "refrigerator repair near me" Main source of high intent calls. Use call extensions and a schedule that matches when you answer.


Local Services Ads Pay per lead listing at the top with a verified badge Phone leads without paying per click. Eligibility depends on your area and category, so check Google's list.


Google Business Profile Map listing with reviews, hours, photos and a call button Free. Keep hours, service area and review replies current.


Facebook and Instagram ads Reaches homeowners in your service area before and after a breakdown Local awareness, a standing offer, and reminders to save your number.


Referrals and repeat customers Past customers, landlords, property managers, realtors Magnet on the repaired machine, follow up text, and a simple thank you for referrals.


If you are choosing one paid channel first, pick Google Search or Local Services Ads. ## Where Meta ads fit


Nobody scrolls Facebook looking for a dryer technician. So Meta ads work differently from search. They keep your name in front of local homeowners so that when the washer breaks, your shop is the one they recognize. The ad wall shows that a Meta ad can run for years when the message is stable: experience, area, price and a phone number.


A simple setup works for most shops.


- Target a radius around your real service area, not the whole metro.
- Use one image of a tech at work or a finished repair, or a short video of a tech explaining a common symptom.
- Set the button to Call now.
- Keep one standing offer, such as a service call fee applied to the repair.
- Leave the ad running and refresh the image every few months.


## Appliance repair ad copy you can adapt


Replace the town, years and prices with your own. Only state what you can deliver.


### Google Search ad


Responsive search ads allow headlines of up to 30 characters.


Element Copy Characters


Headline 1 Appliance Repair in Tacoma 26


Headline 2 Same Day Service Available 26


Headline 3 30 Years Fixing Appliances 26


Headline 4 Call Now, Speak to a Person 27


Description 1 Fridge, washer, dryer, oven and dishwasher repair. Service call from $75. 73


### Facebook and Instagram ad


"Refrigerator not keeping food fresh? Oven not heating? Our techs have been repairing appliances in Tacoma and Puyallup for 30 years. Call today and we will tell you when we can be there. Service call starts at $75." Image: a tech with a toolkit at a customer's door. Button: Call now.


### Goodwill offer


"Veterans: your service call is on us. Call us for any appliance repair and mention this ad." A waived fee is small to you and memorable to them. Set a clear limit, such as the service call fee only, so the offer stays affordable.


## The math: what a lead is worth


Appliance repair leads cost money, so work out what a booked job is worth before you set a budget. Here is a worked example with round numbers. Replace them with your own.


Step Number


Monthly ad budget $1,500


Cost per phone call $45


Calls generated 33


Share of calls booked as jobs 60%


Jobs booked 20


Ad cost per booked job $75


Average ticket $240


Gross profit per job at 55% $132


Profit per job after ad cost $57


At those numbers the campaign makes about $1,140 after ad spend, from 20 jobs. Now see what happens if you answer more calls. If your booking rate rises from 60% to 75%, the same 33 calls become about 25 jobs. Cost per booked job falls to $60, and profit per job rises to $72. A better phone process can matter as much as a better ad.


Repeat customers add to this. A homeowner who had a good washer repair will call you for the dryer next year. Count that as upside, but do not rely on it when you set the budget.


## Answering the phone is part of the marketing


Because most leads arrive as calls, your phone handling is part of your lead generation. Small fixes often raise booked jobs without raising spend.


- **Answer in a few rings.** If the office is busy, forward calls to a mobile or a service that answers for you.
- **Call back missed calls fast.** A text that says "Sorry we missed you, we can be there tomorrow morning" can save the job.
- **State the fee and the window.** "Service call is $75, applied to the repair, and I can be there between 1 and 3."
- **Ask what the machine is doing.** Brand, model, symptom. It shows competence and lets you bring the right part.
- **Match ad hours to staffed hours.** If nobody answers at night, schedule ads or call extensions to pause.


## How to measure appliance repair advertising


Track three numbers each month: calls from each source, jobs booked from those calls, and ad spend. Divide spend by jobs booked to get cost per booked job. Then compare it with gross profit per job.


Use call tracking numbers or the call reporting in Google Ads so you can tell which channel rang the phone. Mark each new call as booked, quote only or wrong number. Wrong numbers and parts inquiries show up in any account, and a cost per call that ignores them looks better than it is.


Review the numbers monthly, not daily. A few slow days after a cold snap or a holiday tell you little. Look at the search terms report for words such as "parts" or "manual" and add them as negative keywords so you stop paying for people who want to fix it themselves.

## FAQ


### How do appliance repair shops get leads?


Most leads come from Google Search, Local Services Ads where available, and a complete Google Business Profile, because people search at the moment a machine breaks. Meta ads, referrals and repeat customers add to that. Most of these leads arrive as phone calls.


### What should an appliance repair ad say?


Say your years in business, the towns you serve, a starting service call price and one action, usually Call now. The long-running ads on the ad wall follow this pattern. Skip long lists of every brand and machine.


### Do Facebook ads work for appliance repair?


They can, in a supporting role. Facebook and Instagram keep your name in front of local homeowners, so you are the shop they remember when something breaks. Search catches the people who are looking right now. Use a tight radius, a Call now button and one steady offer.


### How much does an appliance repair lead cost?


It depends on your market and channel, so work from your own account. Divide spend by calls, then by jobs booked. Compare cost per booked job to gross profit per job. If a job leaves you $130 in gross profit and costs $75 in ads to win, the campaign pays.


### Are Local Services Ads worth it for appliance repair?


They can be, where your category and area are eligible. You pay per lead, the listing sits at the top of the page, and a verified badge builds trust. Check Google's eligibility list and compare cost per booked job against your search ads.
